name: MongoDB
recipe: None. mongod is a ~5M-LOC multithreaded C++ server. Hard blockers, each independently fatal for wasm32-wasi/wasmtime: (1) network-as-purpose — it IS a TCP server (listen/accept/sockets), the entire value prop is a remote DB daemon; wasi has no sockets in our model. (2) native threads — WiredTiger storage engine + replication + connection-per-thread architecture rely on pthreads/std::thread; no native threads in single-threaded wasm sandbox. (3) embedded JS engine (SpiderMonkey/V8) for $where/mapReduce/$function — JIT, fork-exec-style, not portable. (4) build is cmake/SCons-driven multi-tarball with codegen (IDL compiler, generated BSON/feature-flag headers); not pregenerated, violates lane-B no-configure/no-codegen. (5) mmap/fork, async IO, fsync semantics WiredTiger expects. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi mongod exists (lane A miss). Not a single Rust crate (lane C N/A). Not Python/JS-on-QuickJS (lane D N/A). For embedded document-store needs the LIVE sqlite3 (with JSON1) already covers the BSON/JSON-record use case in-sandbox.
smoke: N/A — impossible. (Counterfactual: if a wasm32-wasi mongod existed, `wasmtime mongod --version` then start mongod, `mongosh --eval 'db.t.insertOne({a:1}); db.t.findOne()'` — but it requires a TCP listener + threads wasmtime cannot provide.)
blocker: Network-as-purpose (TCP server daemon) + native multithreading (WiredTiger/replication) + embedded JS JIT engine + codegen-driven cmake/SCons build. Any one is fatal under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime; all four present. sqlite3+JSON1 already LIVE covers the embedded document-store need.

name: FoundationDB
recipe: No viable recipe. FoundationDB is a distributed multi-process KV store. Its value is a cluster of cooperating processes (coordinators, storage servers, transaction logs) coordinated by Flow, a custom C++ actor/coroutine runtime built directly on epoll-based async networking. The server (fdbserver) and the C client (libfdb_c) both center the network engine: the client is a TCP client to a remote cluster, the server is one node in a networked cluster. None of this reduces to a self-contained, deterministic, single-process wasm32-wasi computation. Lane B is out: Flow generates code via its actorcompiler and the build hard-depends on epoll/sockets/threads/fork-exec, not pure libc++. Lane A/C/D do not apply (massive C++, not a prebuilt .wasm, not a bare Rust crate, not pure-Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — no in-sandbox build attempted. The architecture (network-as-purpose, multi-process cluster, native threads, epoll, fork-exec) is disqualifying on its face. Even a single-process fdbserver still runs the Flow network loop, so there is no smoke test that exercises FDB value without networking.
blocker: Network-as-purpose distributed system: Flow actor runtime over epoll networking, multi-process cluster requiring fork-exec + native threads. No single-process embeddable mode delivers the product's value (distributed strict serializability). All disqualify wasm32-wasi standalone under wasmtime. For embedded transactional KV, sqlite3 is already LIVE.

name: TimescaleDB
blocker: TimescaleDB is a PostgreSQL C extension (.so loaded by `shared_preload_libraries`) — it has no standalone existence; it requires a running Postgres backend, hooks into Postgres planner/executor internals, and uses background workers (the telemetry/job scheduler bgw launcher), shared memory, and the Postgres process model. Postgres itself only barely runs in WASM via pglite (Emscripten, single-user, NO background workers, NO bgworkers, NO shared_preload_libraries extension loading). TimescaleDB depends precisely on the features pglite strips. Not a self-contained C library: it is dlopen'd into Postgres and unbuildable as a freestanding wasm32-wasi .wasm. No prebuilt wasm exists; can't be a bare Rust crate (it's C) or pure-Python/JS. fork-exec/bgworker/shared-memory process model = impossible under wasmtime single-process model.

name: Couchbase
recipe: No recipe. Couchbase Server is a multi-process clustered distributed database: Erlang/OTP (BEAM VM) cluster manager + C/C++ data service (memcached-derived) + Go N1QL/SQL++ query and index services, communicating over the network with disk persistence, vBucket sharding (1024 partitions), and replication. No wasm32-wasi build exists and none is feasible — it requires a multi-language runtime (BEAM scheduler with native threads, Go runtime with goroutine threading/netpoller), fork-exec of separate service binaries, and TCP networking as its core purpose. None of the four lanes apply: A (no prebuilt wasm), B (not self-contained C/C++ — it is BEAM+Go+C across services and is network-clustered), C (not a Rust crate), D (not Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — no buildable single-binary slice. Even the C/C++ data service is memcached-derived and exists to serve a network protocol within a cluster, not as a standalone in-sandbox lib.
blocker: Network-as-purpose clustered DB; multi-process fork-exec of separate Erlang/C++/Go service binaries; requires BEAM VM + Go runtime native threads and TCP networking. No wasm32-wasi build; not portable to standalone wasm under wasmtime.

name: RethinkDB
recipe: None. RethinkDB is a large C++ server (~250k LOC) with a custom B-tree storage engine, the ReQL query engine, and a long-lived TCP server whose entire reason for existing is realtime changefeeds pushed to connected clients over the network. No wasm32-wasi build exists. It depends on a thread-per-core / coroutine event loop (its own arch-specific context-switch asm in the "arch" runtime), native sockets, and persistent server processes — all of which violate the in-sandbox model (network-as-purpose, native threads, long-lived server). Not lane A (no prebuilt wasm), not B (not self-contained; needs threads + sockets + huge configure/codegen + protobuf), not C (C++ not Rust), not D (not Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — no buildable or runnable target. Conceptually: `rethinkdb` boots a server bound to a TCP port (28015/29015) and serves changefeeds; there is nothing meaningful to invoke as a one-shot stdin→stdout wasm command.
blocker: Network-as-purpose: core value is a long-lived TCP changefeed/push server. Also requires native threads (thread-per-core + custom context-switch asm) and a custom storage engine. No wasm build; inherently a networked server, not a sandboxable one-shot command.

name: ArangoDB
recipe: N/A — cannot run in-sandbox as standalone wasm32-wasi.
blocker: Large C++ server embedding V8 (a JIT engine that won't run jitless under wasmtime) for AQL/Foxx execution, plus RocksDB storage and a clustered network database server whose entire purpose is network service. No wasm build exists. JIT + network-as-purpose + native-thread/clustered-server all independently disqualify it. Not a single-binary computational tool — it is a stateful DB server.

name: Greenplum
smoke: N/A — no viable single-instance wasm build. The only conceivable "smoke" (start coordinator + segments, run a parallel query) requires the very networked multi-process cluster that is forbidden in-sandbox.
blocker: Greenplum is a heavily-modified Postgres fork whose ENTIRE value proposition is massively-parallel processing (MPP): a coordinator process distributes queries across many segment hosts (each itself a modified postgres instance) coordinated over a TCP/UDP interconnect (gpfdist/Motion nodes). This requires: (1) fork-exec of multiple postmaster/segment processes, (2) the network interconnect as the core purpose (segment-to-segment Motion shuffles), (3) multiple cooperating OS processes with shared-memory + semaphores. All three are categorically out-of-bounds for a single standalone wasm32-wasi module under wasmtime (no fork-exec, no network-as-purpose, no real multi-process/threads). Even plain single-instance Postgres "barely runs" in wasm and needs heavy patching (no fork — postgres relies on fork() per backend); Greenplum strictly adds the MPP layer on top, making it strictly harder. Single-instance MPP is a contradiction in terms — strip the parallelism and you have nothing left of Greenplum's value. Massive C codebase (~1M+ LOC), configure-based build, fork/process model, network interconnect. Not lane A (no prebuilt wasm exists), not B (fork-exec + network core, not self-contained single-instance), not C/D (it's C, not Rust/Python/JS). Note: in-sandbox SQL/analytics is already covered by LIVE sqlite3 for the single-instance case.

name: TerminusDB
recipe: No viable recipe. TerminusDB is a Prolog/Rust hybrid: terminusdb-store (Rust) is only the storage engine, while the actual database — query language (WOQL), schema/document logic, transactions, HTTP API — is implemented in SWI-Prolog and drives the Rust store via C-FFI (terminus_store_prolog). You cannot ship "just the Rust store" as the database; without the Prolog layer there is no DB, only a triple-store library with no query/logic. The Rust store alone is a Lane C candidate but it is a large multi-crate workspace with proc-macros and depends on the Prolog host to be a database, so it is useless in isolation. The Prolog layer cannot be brought into wasm32-wasi: SWI-Prolog's only wasm port (swipl-wasm / npm-swipl-wasm) targets Emscripten + a browser VM with JS glue, not standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime. SWI-Prolog is a large C runtime with its own GC, dynamic foreign-resource loading, threading, and signal/setjmp machinery that the Emscripten port leans on; there is no wasm32-wasi target. Both halves fail: Rust half is not-a-database, Prolog half is browser-emscripten-only.
smoke: N/A — no buildable standalone module. (Hypothetical disproof: `swipl --version` cannot be produced as a wasm32-wasi command since the only wasm SWI-Prolog build is Emscripten/browser, requiring JS glue + a browser/Node host, not wasmtime.)
blocker: Database logic/query layer is SWI-Prolog, a large C runtime whose only wasm port is Emscripten/browser-targeted (needs JS glue + browser/Node VM), not standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime. The Rust terminusdb-store is only the storage engine driven by Prolog over FFI — not a database on its own — so neither half yields a runnable in-sandbox module.

name: Aerospike
recipe: N/A — cannot build or run as wasm32-wasi.
smoke: N/A — no viable in-sandbox target. (Theoretical only: a no-network single-shard storage core would be a months-long fork yielding a different product, not Aerospike.)
blocker: Aerospike is a 64-bit GNU/Linux-only clustered distributed KV store whose entire value IS the platform-pinned capabilities wasm32-wasi cannot expose: networking/clustering is the product's purpose (network-as-purpose -> impossible), raw block-device direct IO (O_DIRECT) for its hybrid DRAM+SSD storage, SysV shared memory, native pthread multithreading, and jemalloc. C99 server (94% C, 3.6% C++) with autoconf/automake/cmake + S2 (abseil-cpp), Lua, jansson, libbacktrace, yaml-cpp, OpenSSL submodules — not a single-binary self-contained source tree. No prebuilt wasm exists. Disqualified on multiple independent grounds (network, raw device IO, threads, shmem). The C "could theoretically compile" but the running product cannot exist without these syscalls.

name: DragonflyDB
recipe: N/A — cannot build or run as wasm32-wasi under wasmtime.
smoke: N/A — no buildable single-file artifact exists for the sandbox.
blocker: Multiple hard blockers, any one fatal for wasip1/wasmtime: (1) io_uring async IO — Linux-kernel-specific, unavailable in WASI; (2) shared-nothing MULTI-THREADED architecture (Helio thread-per-shard) — wasip1 has no threads; (3) network-server IS the purpose — Redis/Memcached wire protocol over TCP, disallowed network-as-purpose; (4) large C++ codebase (~73% C++) on CMake with Helio + Boost-style fibers/sockets, far beyond Lane B self-contained C/C++. Not a prebuilt wasm tool (Lane A), not Rust (C), not Python/JS (D).

name: Tarantool
blocker: Network database server by purpose (TCP listener / iproto protocol is the whole point — network-as-purpose). Multiple independent hard blockers stack on top: (1) bundles LuaJIT, whose value IS its JIT = runtime native-code emission, which wasm forbids (immutable code memory, no in-wasm codegen); it would only fall back to plain interpretation, defeating its purpose; (2) fiber engine uses setjmp/longjmp / hand-written context-switch asm (not portable to wasm32-wasi, which lacks setjmp/longjmp and stack-switching); (3) epoll/libev-style event loop for the network reactor; (4) large autotools/CMake C codebase with platform-specific assembly and configure-time codegen. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists. Not a standalone in-sandbox compute tool — it is a server. Not covered by the LIVE list (live lua is PUC-Lua interpreter, a different thing). Verdict: impossible.

name: Apache Kudu
recipe: N/A — no in-sandbox build path. Kudu is a distributed C++ storage engine (master + tablet servers, Raft consensus replication, RPC networking). Its value is the clustered, replicated, networked storage tier integrated with Impala/Spark/Flink — not a single embeddable library. Requires native threads, fork-exec, and network-as-purpose, all of which are forbidden under standalone wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. No prebuilt wasm, no self-contained single-lib C/C++ mode, not Rust, not Python/JS.
smoke: None possible — there is no single-process embeddable artifact to run. A meaningful smoke (create table, insert, columnar scan) inherently requires a running master + tablet server cluster over the network.
blocker: network-as-purpose (Raft replication + RPC between master/tablet servers) plus native-thread and fork-exec dependence; no embeddable single-lib mode — the clustered networked storage tier IS the product.

name: pgvector
recipe: N/A — pgvector is a PostgreSQL C extension (PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 API), not a standalone program or library. It compiles against Postgres server headers and loads as a .so via Postgres's dynamic loader; its only entry point is `CREATE EXTENSION vector` inside a running backend. To "run" it you must first port full PostgreSQL to wasm32-wasi, which is the real blocker: Postgres uses the fork() postmaster/backend process model plus SysV/POSIX shared memory and process-based concurrency — none available under wasi-preview1/wasmtime (no fork-exec, no shared-memory IPC). The only existing Postgres-to-wasm path is PGlite via Emscripten, which is a browser/single-user Asyncify build, NOT a plain wasm32-wasi CLI, and depends on the Emscripten JS runtime/FS shim. That fails the no-browser and no-fork-exec constraints. No Lane B self-contained build either, since pgvector cannot link or run without the Postgres server it extends.
smoke: None possible. pgvector has no standalone CLI or library smoke; the only invocation is `CREATE EXTENSION vector; SELECT '[1,2,3]'::vector <-> '[4,5,6]'::vector;` executed inside a live Postgres backend, which itself cannot run under wasmtime/wasi.
blocker: pgvector is meaningless without full PostgreSQL, and Postgres cannot run as wasm32-wasi under wasmtime: it depends on fork() (postmaster/backend process model), SysV/POSIX shared memory, and process-based concurrency — all absent in wasi-preview1. The only Postgres-to-wasm path (PGlite) is Emscripten/browser (Asyncify + JS FS shim), not a plain wasi CLI, violating the no-browser/no-fork-exec rules.

name: Apache Hudi
blocker:
Reference Hudi is JVM/Spark/Hadoop-coupled (JIT-bound, not wasm). The only non-JVM path, hudi-rs, is a large multi-crate Rust workspace whose purpose is reading/writing tables over network object storage (object_store with AWS/Azure/GCP). It depends on arrow ~54 + parquet + datafusion@45 (huge, edition 2021, proc-macro and trait-heavy) and a multi-threaded tokio runtime. mrustc ~1.74 (Lane C) cannot build arrow/datafusion/tokio (size, proc-macros, native threads). Network-as-purpose + native-threads + JIT all independently disqualify. Not covered by any LIVE component.</blocker>

No source to compile (kills Lane B), no prebuilt .wasm (kills Lane A), not Rust/Python/JS (kills C/D). Also mmap + threads/network in sync builds would violate sandbox even with source. name: Realm
blocker: Only demonstrated wasm build is an Emscripten BROWSER target (realm-js alpha, nh/wasm/emscripten_target) needing a JS/DOM host + Asyncify; per MongoDB docs it stores local data IN-MEMORY ONLY because the on-disk engine does not work there. Realm Core (C++) on-disk engine needs mmap + cross-process/thread file locking (robust mutexes in shared memory) for its MVCC/commit-log design, plus pthreads for sync. None map to standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime (no shared-memory robust mutexes, no multi-process locking, no pthreads). Product PURPOSE is Atlas Device Sync = network-as-purpose, impossible by rule. Browser/Emscripten artifact is not wasm32-wasi standalone. Lane B fails (needs OS threads+locking, not just self-contained C++); no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm for Lane A. Already-LIVE sqlite3 covers in-sandbox embedded DB.

name: libreoffice (soffice)
recipe: No viable recipe. LibreOffice is a ~10M-LOC C++ suite built with a bespoke gbuild system and dozens of bundled native externals (ICU, Boost, Skia, NSS, cppunit). The only existing wasm port (ZetaOffice/Allotropia) is Emscripten + Qt5 + pthreads/SharedArrayBuffer + WebGL — a browser/GPU/native-threads target, not wasm32-wasi. Headless soffice --convert-to pdf still depends on the UNO component model (dlopen of .so plugin components), fork/exec of helper processes, and threading. None of this is expressible as a self-contained C/C++ wasm32-wasi tarball (Lane B), a prebuilt .wasm (A), a Rust crate (C), or pure-Python/JS (D).
smoke: N/A — not buildable for wasmtime. If hypothetically built: printf 'hi' > a.odt; soffice --headless --convert-to pdf a.odt; test -f a.pdf. Cannot run: requires fork/exec, dlopen of UNO components, and native threads.
blocker: Requires native threads (pthreads/SharedArrayBuffer), fork-exec of subprocesses, and dlopen of UNO .so component plugins; only wasm port is Emscripten+Qt5+WebGL browser-only, not wasm32-wasi. ~10M-LOC C++ with custom build system and many native externals — not a self-contained tarball.

name: inkscape
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. Inkscape is a multi-hundred-kLOC GTK/C++ desktop GUI application. Even the headless CLI export path (--export-type=png/pdf) links the full editor core, cairo, pango, GLib/GObject/GIO, libxml2, Boost, and the GTK/GDK stack, and shells out to Python/Perl extension subprocesses via fork-exec. No mainline or community wasm32-wasi build exists. Not lane A (no prebuilt wasm), not B (sprawling autotools/meson C++ with GObject + GUI deps, fork-exec extensions), not C (not Rust), not D (not pure-Python/JS). For the underlying need (SVG-to-PNG/PDF) the closer target would be librsvg — but that is Rust depending on cairo/pango/GObject (C libs) and is itself not mrustc-viable.
smoke: N/A — nothing to build. If a candidate existed: wasmtime run inkscape.wasm --export-type=png --export-filename=out.png in.svg; assert out.png is a valid PNG. Not attemptable.

name: PyTorch
recipe: No viable recipe. libtorch/ATen is a massive native C++ codebase (op dispatcher generated by Python codegen at build time, autograd engine, caffe2 multithreaded threadpool, intra-op parallelism, MKL/oneDNN BLAS, optional CUDA) with no maintained wasm32-wasi target. Lane B fails: build is CMake + generative codegen (not pre-generated/self-contained), and core relies on native pthreads thread pool + BLAS intrinsics with no clean single-threaded WASI fallback. Lane A: the only PyTorch+wasm artifact in existence is the wasi-nn 'PyTorch backend' (Wasmtime 27 --features pytorch / WasmEdge), which runs libtorch NATIVELY on the HOST as a runtime plugin and exposes inference to the guest over the wasi-nn import boundary -- that is host-side native execution, not standalone in-sandbox wasm, so it is disqualified. ExecuTorch (the on-device offshoot) is a separate native runtime, likewise no wasm32-wasi standalone build. Lanes C (Rust) and D (pure-Python) are inapplicable.
smoke: N/A -- no in-sandbox build is producible. (Hypothetical smoke would be `python -c "import torch; print(torch.tensor([1,2,3]).sum())"` -> 6, but torch has no wasm32-wasi wheel and no native pip C-extension can be built for the sandbox.)
blocker: Native multithreaded C++ (caffe2 threadpool + intra-op parallelism, MKL/oneDNN BLAS), build-time Python codegen of the ATen dispatcher (not pre-generated, so violates self-contained C/C++ lane), and no maintained wasm32-wasi target. The only existing PyTorch+wasm path (wasi-nn backend) runs libtorch as a NATIVE host plugin called over import boundaries -- native exec, disqualified. ExecuTorch is a separate native runtime, not standalone wasm.
